title.en: Show the effect of transactions on assets, liabilities and capital

say.en: Whatever a business does, buying, selling or paying, one equation always stays true. Let us test it with a real set of transactions. In this lesson: State the accounting equation.
Show the effect of transactions on assets, liabilities and capital.

body.en: Based on the dual aspect concept, the resources of a business (assets) always equal the claims on them: the claims of outsiders (liabilities) and of the owner (capital). Revenue and profit increase capital; expenses, losses and drawings decrease it. Every transaction changes the *equation*, but the two sides always remain equal.
body.kn: ದ್ವಿಮುಖ ಪರಿಕಲ್ಪನೆಯ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಆಸ್ತಿಗಳು ಯಾವಾಗಲೂ ಹೊಣೆಗಾರಿಕೆ ಮತ್ತು ಬಂಡವಾಳದ ಮೊತ್ತಕ್ಕೆ ಸಮ. ಆದಾಯ ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ವೆಚ್ಚ ಮತ್ತು ಸೆಳೆತ ಅದನ್ನು ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ.

title.en: On the board: Raj's accounting equation

say.en: Raj starts with 2 lakh cash: cash, an asset, equals his capital.
Goods on credit raise stock and creditors. Buying furniture for cash just swaps one asset for another.
Goods costing 20 thousand sold for 28 thousand: the profit of 8 thousand raises capital.
Rent paid and drawings both reduce cash and capital.
Add the columns: assets 2,51,000 equal creditors 50,000 plus capital 2,01,000.
On the board: Raj's accounting equation.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. Show the accounting equation for Raj: (1) started business with cash ₹2,00,000; (2) bought goods on credit from Sunil ₹50,000; (3) bought furniture for cash ₹30,000; (4) sold goods costing ₹20,000 for ₹28,000 cash; (5) paid rent ₹4,000; (6) withdrew ₹3,000 for personal use.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. Show the accounting equation for Raj: 1 started business with cash 2,00,000 rupees; 2 bought goods on credit from Sunil 50,000 rupees; 3 bought furniture for cash 30,000 rupees; 4 sold goods costing 20,000 rupees for 28,000 rupees cash; 5 paid rent 4,000 rupees; 6 withdrew 3,000 rupees for personal use.
1 Cash 2,00,000 equals Capital 2,00,000.
2 Stock plus 50,000; Creditors plus 50,000 gives Assets 2,50,000 equals L 50,000 plus C 2,00,000.
3 Cash minus 30,000; Furniture plus 30,000 gives totals unchanged.
4 Cash plus 28,000; Stock minus 20,000; Capital plus 8,000 profit gives Assets 2,58,000 equals L 50,000 plus C 2,08,000.
5 Cash minus 4,000; Capital minus 4,000. 6 Cash minus 3,000; Capital minus 3,000.
Final: Cash 1,91,000 plus Stock 30,000 plus Furniture 30,000 equals 2,51,000 equals Creditors 50,000 plus Capital 2,01,000.
So the answer is Assets 2,51,000 rupees equals Liabilities 50,000 rupees plus Capital 2,01,000 rupees.

body.en: Ask two questions for every transaction: which items change, and does the owner gain or lose? Gains and losses always go to capital; everything else stays among assets and liabilities.
